page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates all placing in the top tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory and CPU scores, also demonstrate average tier performance. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative weakness, scoring in the bottom 25%, and medium-model LLM prompt processing lands in the bottom 10%.

Given its dedicated hardware allocation and balanced resource profile, the D4as_v7 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require strong single-threaded execution without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The absence of local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale remote Premium Storage independently. This server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, text processing, software compilation, and light database operations.
